chosen.title: The Data Broker State: How the FBI, DHS, and a $315 Billion Industry Built the Surveillance Machine Nobody Voted For
chosen.rationale: In 2026 federal surveillance-by-purchase went from rumor to confirmed practice: FBI Director Kash Patel told Congress in March the Bureau is buying Americans' location histories from data brokers, DHS now runs on $165B in yearly funding, and the broker market itself sits near $315B and growing — even as Congress floats the 269-page GAAIA framework and Illinois signs its own AI Safety Measures Act. It's the exact 'follow the money, name who profits' story that's currently unresolved in the news cycle, and it hasn't been touched by any AIMA title to date.

sources.name: The Conversation / NYU IFP — US government ramps up mass surveillance with help of AI tech, data brokers

rejected_candidates.title: The AI Alibi: How Companies Learned to Blame the Algorithm for Layoffs They'd Have Made Anyway
rejected_candidates.rationale: The 'AI washing' debate has sharpened through mid-2026: 56% of this year's 267 layoff events cite AI, roughly 50,000 jobs' worth, even as the same firms post record revenue — and Gallup just found 62% of the workers actually laid off were non-users of AI, undercutting the official narrative. It's a live, data-backed instance of corporations using automation as rhetorical cover, distinct from AIMA's existing labor pieces (which cover the global labor shift and gig economy, not the deception framing itself) and squarely in Dawn's 'follow the money' register.

rejected_candidates.title: The Bedside Bias: What Happens When the Algorithm Decides You Don't Need as Much Care
rejected_candidates.rationale: A Cedars-Sinai-led study found leading LLMs — Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, and others — generate measurably less aggressive treatment recommendations when a patient is coded as Black, echoing parallel findings that AI image tools score Black women's natural hairstyles as less 'professional' in hiring contexts. It's fresh clinical evidence with teeth for algorithmic bias in medicine specifically, distinct from AIMA's existing 'Diagnosis by Algorithm' industry-state piece by focusing on racial bias in the recommendation itself rather than adoption trends.
